# Audio test fixtures (#155)

Short, committed clips for the `nmg_game_dev.audio` tests. Each is well under 50 KB. The tests never
call ElevenLabs and never open a live editor, so these files are the only audio input.

| File | Contents | How it was made |
|------|----------|-----------------|
| `tone.wav` | 0.25 s, 440 Hz sine, mono, 22050 Hz, signed 16-bit PCM | `soundfile` (libsndfile) writes WAV/PCM_16 |
| `tone.mp3` | 0.25 s, 440 Hz sine, mono, 22050 Hz, MPEG-1/2 Layer III | `soundfile` writes MP3 (LAME) |
| `tone.ogg` | 0.25 s, stereo, 32000 Hz, Ogg Vorbis (330 Hz left, 495 Hz right) | `soundfile` writes OGG/VORBIS |
| `tone.flac` | 0.25 s, stereo, 48000 Hz, FLAC 16-bit (262 Hz left, 392 Hz right) | `soundfile` writes FLAC/PCM_16 |
| `corrupt.mp3` | 1536 bytes of ASCII text under an `.mp3` name | Repeated text, cut to 1536 bytes; not an audio stream |

The rates and channel counts differ on purpose. Each decoded WAV must keep its source rate and
channel count, so a decoder that falls back to miniaudio's 44100 Hz stereo default fails the tests.

Regenerate the valid clips with (from the repository root):

```bash
uv run --no-project --with soundfile --with numpy python - tests/fixtures/audio <<'PY'
import math, os, sys
import numpy as np
import soundfile as sf

out = sys.argv[1]
dur = 0.25

def tone(rate, channels, freqs):
    t = np.arange(int(rate * dur)) / rate
    cols = [0.4 * np.sin(2 * math.pi * f * t) for f in freqs[:channels]]
    return np.stack(cols, axis=1) if channels > 1 else cols[0]

specs = {
    "tone.wav": ("WAV", "PCM_16", 22050, 1, (440.0,)),
    "tone.mp3": ("MP3", "MPEG_LAYER_III", 22050, 1, (440.0,)),
    "tone.ogg": ("OGG", "VORBIS", 32000, 2, (330.0, 495.0)),
    "tone.flac": ("FLAC", "PCM_16", 48000, 2, (262.0, 392.0)),
}
for name, (fmt, subtype, rate, channels, freqs) in specs.items():
    sf.write(os.path.join(out, name), tone(rate, channels, freqs), rate, format=fmt, subtype=subtype)
PY
```

The WAV, MP3, and FLAC clips come back byte for byte. The OGG clip keeps its rate, channels, and
length, but its bytes differ between encodes.

`corrupt.mp3` is not regenerated by that script. It is the text `This is not an MP3 stream. ` repeated
and cut to 1536 bytes.
